Cuman Hungarian marriage pasture and service
RagShortTexts: Cumans have marriage and service ties with Hungary’s royalty.
Pasture and local jurisdiction can still cause disputes.

Variants.Content: Cuman-Hungarian royal marriage and service ties offer protection and military partnership but involve pasture, settlers and local authority. Agreements need acceptance from herders and landholders; kin prestige cannot settle access to water or disputes alone.
Cuman riders need forage and places for dependants. Joint signals and assembly require agreement; royal marriage does not train unfamiliar contingents to act together.
Royal cavalry alliances need workable livelihoods and neighboring land claims resolved. Promised service without pasture arrangements turns costs into local conflict.
Herd routes can meet cultivated fields, requiring mediation over damage. Households judge royal cooperation by compensation and dependable local safety.
